instructions.task: Does own still require a new answer from the reader?

criteria.true: The section's own words require a new answer now, including an implicit request that brings a currently unsettled proposal to the reader. A reference to answering an earlier control still requests an answer; the control's presence does not mean the owner has answered.
criteria.false: The section itself only explains, reports a source-recorded settled decision, records the author's assumptions without requesting an answer, or asks only for comments. An explicit source-recorded answer settling the same choice means no new answer is required even if older pick/open wording remains.

instructions.task: Do same_file_controls serve every new answer that own requests?

criteria.true: The native controls match each requested question and its answer semantics, including an explicit reference to answering above or earlier on this page. A matching control need not share this heading.
criteria.false: At least one currently requested answer has no corresponding native control in the list. A control for a different question, or a comparison without an answer control, does not serve it.

reference.boundary: Only own can introduce the answer request being assessed. parent and full can supply its antecedent or status; a different request in the parent is not a request in every explanatory child. A proposal alone is not a request. Source-recorded acceptance of the same choice settles older open/pick wording; an initial selection, a local saved response and a recommendation do not. same_file_controls lists the actual native controls on this page in source order, including controls under other headings. A request can legitimately refer to a matching control above; unrelated controls do not serve it.

no.finding: This section requests a new answer, but the page has no native choice control; inspect the request and the matching guide's answer component.
This section requests a new answer that no same-page native choice serves; inspect the request and the listed controls.

instructions.task: Does control ask this reader to settle a currently open consequential choice or a relied-on unproven assumption described in context?

criteria.true: An answer accepts or changes a consequential design/product choice, a premise the work relies on, its failure consequences or the required proof. Confirmation is included when it authorizes that outcome. A multiple-answer control is included if any answer does so.
criteria.false: Every answer is only nonconsequential procedure, feedback or comprehension that authorizes no such outcome; a hypothetical example; or a choice explicitly settled by source-recorded owner acceptance. Initial selection and local saved response alone do not establish acceptance.

instructions.task: Does preceding explain the decision, problem or relied-on assumption that this control asks the reader to answer?

criteria.true: The preceding section text or heading identifies the concrete issue, choice or premise, so the reader knows what the options concern.
criteria.false: Only the control names the issue, or the preceding section text never identifies it.

instructions.task: Anywhere in this same section, including the control's own options and later text, does it explain what each alternative gains?

criteria.true: Each alternative has a concrete benefit, stated directly or clear from an unambiguous effect explained in the section. No benefit label or separate comparison is required.
criteria.false: For at least one alternative, its benefit is absent from the entire section, including its option explanation.

instructions.task: Anywhere in this same section, including the control's own options and later text, does it explain what each alternative costs?

criteria.true: Each alternative has a concrete cost, risk or sacrificed benefit, stated directly or clear from an unambiguous effect explained in the section.
criteria.false: For at least one alternative, its cost, risk or sacrificed benefit is absent from the entire section, including its option explanation.

instructions.task: Anywhere in this same section, including the control's options, does it identify who bears each cost? If plausible readers would disagree who pays and the section does not settle it, keep that assessment uncertain rather than declaring absence.

criteria.true: Every cost has a stated bearer or one unambiguous role/effect connection that identifies who pays; a personal name is not required.
criteria.false: A clearly described cost has no supplied bearer, either stated or unambiguously connected by role/effect. Genuine ambiguity about a plausible bearer is not this known-absence case.

instructions.task: Anywhere in this same section, including the control's options and later text, is the author's recommended, proposed or retained position identifiable with its reasons?

criteria.true: The authored explanation identifies a current author position and why, whether called recommended or clearly proposed/retained. An option title can recommend it, with its explanation supplying reasons.
criteria.false: The section supplies no identifiable current author position with reasons. Initial selection, a local response, or a historical choice without a current position is insufficient.

reference.status_boundary: control identifies the selected native choice by its id/title. context currently contains all enclosing heading sections and can repeat text. Locate the nearest governing section for this control. An explicit source-recorded owner decision for this same choice, including a heading before it or a later statement, settles older open wording; local selection and recommendation do not. A review of a relied-on assumption or its proof limits can request a consequential answer without choosing a new architecture.
reference.preceding_boundary: preceding is the asking-text projection of the exact stored raw source prefix of the nearest configured containing section: section beginning through this identified control's start, excluding the control and all later bytes. Judge this question only from preceding, using control for identity, not its option content. Available empty is distinct from unavailable/cut; do not replace missing evidence with context from elsewhere. Other fields remain visible in the shared request, but do not supply this preceding property.
reference.section_boundary: For gains, costs, bearers and recommendation, judge the same governing section represented by preceding, including this control's option titles/explanations and any later content in that section. context currently contains all enclosing sections, so locate that section and do not borrow another choice from an ancestor. Gains/costs can be unambiguously explained by effects; do not invent them. Current author position with reasons need not say recommended; initial selection/local response is insufficient. Ambiguous interpretation stays intermediate. Per-option drawings are not required; parsed local picture presence is a separate mechanical condition. Fields in this shared request do not isolate attention.

no.finding: Worth checking: no configured picture precedes this choice in its heading section. This decision may not need a picture, and a useful picture may sit under another heading. Read sunstack-dev/shared-references/owner-decision-brief.md and presentation-html/references/options-and-decisions.md before changing it.
